title: Kissed, Charred Irish Sirloin Skillet
description: A paleo-friendly, one-pot Irish dish featuring charred sirloin steak tips with a glassy-jelly crust.
instructions: Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the bacon slices and cook until crispy, flipping halfway through.
Remove the cooked bacon and set aside, leaving the drippings in the skillet.
Add the sirloin steak tips and cook for 2-3 minutes per side, or until browned.
Remove the sirloin from the skillet and set aside, leaving the drippings in the skillet.
Add the sliced onion to the skillet and cook until caramelized, stirring occasionally.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the flour and stir to combine, cooking for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the Irish stout, scraping the bottom of the skillet.
Return the sirloin to the skillet and spoon some of the sauce over the meat.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and cook for 10-12 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 130°F - 135°F for medium-rare.
Remove the skillet from the oven and brush the sirloin with the softened Kerrygold butter.
Return the skillet to the stovetop and cook over medium heat, spooning the sauce over the sirloin and sprinkling with thyme, salt, and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with thinly sliced green onions.
